clinical_category: Interstitial lung disease care coordination - multidisciplinary diagnosis of suspected IPF
blueprint_topic: Interprofessional coordination for complex pulmonary diagnostic evaluation
stem: A nurse helps coordinate the diagnostic evaluation of a client with newly detected interstitial lung disease who is clinically suspected of having idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). Which approach is supported by the ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT diagnostic guideline?

options.A: Facilitate multidisciplinary discussion among clinicians with ILD expertise, radiology, and pathology as appropriate to the case
options.B: Rely on a single serum biomarker result to distinguish IPF from other interstitial lung diseases
options.C: Have one specialty determine the diagnosis without integrating the client's clinical and imaging information
options.D: Postpone interdisciplinary review until the client has failed treatment for presumed IPF

rationale: A is correct. The official ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT guideline for diagnosis of IPF conditionally suggests multidisciplinary discussion for diagnostic decision-making in patients with newly detected interstitial lung disease who are clinically suspected of having IPF. The guideline emphasizes integration of clinical, radiologic, and when available histopathologic information. It also recommends against using specified serum biomarkers solely to distinguish IPF from other ILDs. The ATS currently lists the 2018 diagnostic guideline among its official guideline implementation resources, alongside the 2022 IPF update. B, C, and D therefore do not reflect the recommended diagnostic approach.
educational_objective: Coordinate multidisciplinary evaluation for suspected IPF so clinical, radiologic, and when relevant pathologic information are integrated rather than relying on an isolated test or specialty opinion.
source_organization: American Thoracic Society (ATS), European Respiratory Society (ERS), Japanese Respiratory Society (JRS), and Asociación Latinoamericana de Tórax (ALAT)
source_document_title: Diagnosis of Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis. An Official ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT Clinical Practice Guideline; current ATS Guideline Implementation Tools
source_version_date: Diagnostic guideline published 2018; ATS continues to list it in current official implementation resources, alongside the 2022 IPF update; currentness checked 2026-08-18
source_locator: 2018 guideline → recommendations for patients with newly detected ILD clinically suspected of IPF: suggest multidisciplinary discussion for diagnostic decision-making; recommend against measuring serum MMP-7, SPD, CCL-18, or KL-6 solely to distinguish IPF from other ILDs. ATS 'Diagnosis of IPF' Guideline Implementation Tools currently lists the full guideline and clinician summary; ATS master guideline index also lists both the 2018 diagnostic guideline and the 2022 IPF update.
source_claim_supported: The official and currently listed ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT diagnostic guideline directly supports multidisciplinary diagnostic discussion for suspected IPF and rejects sole reliance on selected serum biomarkers for distinguishing IPF from other ILDs.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Management of Care client-needs subcategory (15–21% of items), within Safe and Effective Care Environment; this item tests interprofessional coordination and appropriate referral/collaboration during complex diagnostic care.
correction_summary: Total construct rebuild. The source item's generic claim about broad pulmonology-referral triggers lacked an exact authoritative guideline locator. The final item instead tests a specific, source-supported Management of Care decision: multidisciplinary diagnostic coordination for suspected IPF using the official ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT guideline.
audit_findings: No current authoritative source was located that supported the source item's broad list of universal pulmonology-referral triggers as written.
The official ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT IPF diagnostic guideline directly supports multidisciplinary discussion for diagnostic decision-making in suspected IPF.

ATS currently lists the 2018 diagnostic guideline in its official implementation resources and separately lists the 2022 IPF update, supporting current guideline status rather than relying on an abandoned document.
The serum-biomarker distractor is directly excluded by the same diagnostic guideline; the remaining distractors contradict multidisciplinary integration and do not create a second defensible answer.
Independent adversarial second pass found one uniquely correct answer, no state-law or scope overreach, no unsupported referral threshold, no cueing, and no unresolved conflict.
